data.name: Settings_UnknownLanguage
data.value: Unknown language ({0}); using the Windows language.
data.comment: Settings warning when settings.json names a language M-Tool does not have. {0}: the value from the file.

data.name: Settings_LanguageNotSupported
data.value: Language not supported: {0}
data.comment: Error when the user picks a language M-Tool does not have. {0}: the value, made printable.

data.name: Curve_PointCount
data.value: The curve must have {0} points (it has {1}).
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: required number of points. {1}: number of points the curve has.

data.name: Curve_FirstPointThreshold
data.value: The first point is the idle speed and has no threshold.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. The first point of a curve is the fan speed when the chip is idle; it has no temperature threshold.

data.name: Curve_EnvelopeFirstStep
data.value: Safety rule: the first step must start at {0} °C at the latest.
data.comment: SAFETY. Fan curve problem. {0}: highest allowed temperature in degrees Celsius. Keep the number and the unit.

data.name: Curve_EnvelopeSpeed
data.value: Safety rule: at {0} °C the fan must run at {1}% or more (currently {2}%).
data.comment: SAFETY. Fan curve problem. {0}: temperature in degrees Celsius. {1}: minimum fan speed in percent. {2}: the speed the curve has at that temperature, in percent.

data.name: Curve_SpeedRange
data.value: Point {0}: the fan speed must be between 0% and {1}%.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: number of the point, counted from 1 like the rows of the editor. {1}: highest allowed speed in percent.

data.name: Curve_SpeedDecreases
data.value: Point {0}: the fan speed cannot be lower than the previous point.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: number of the point, counted from 1.

data.name: Curve_ThresholdRange
data.value: Point {0}: the threshold must be {1}-{2} °C.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: number of the point, counted from 1. {1} and {2}: lowest and highest allowed threshold in degrees Celsius.

data.name: Curve_ThresholdOrder
data.value: Point {0}: the threshold must be higher than the previous point's.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: number of the point, counted from 1.

data.name: Curve_DownThreshold
data.value: Point {0}: the fan drops back from this point at {1} °C, which is not above the previous point's threshold ({2} °C). Raise this point's threshold.
data.comment: Fan curve problem. {0}: number of the point, counted from 1. {1}: temperature in degrees Celsius at which the fan leaves this step. {2}: threshold of the previous point in degrees Celsius.

data.name: Curve_LastStepStart
data.value: Safety rule: the last step must start at {0} °C at the latest.
data.comment: SAFETY. Fan curve problem. {0}: highest allowed temperature in degrees Celsius. Keep the number and the unit.

data.name: Curve_LastStepSpeed
data.value: Safety rule: the last step must be at least {0}%.
data.comment: SAFETY. Fan curve problem. {0}: minimum fan speed of the last step, in percent.

data.name: Library_TooMany
data.value: There can be at most {0} custom profiles; delete one first.
data.comment: Error when adding a custom fan profile. {0}: the limit.

data.name: Library_BuiltInReadOnly
data.value: "{0}" is a built-in profile and cannot be changed; copy it and edit the copy.
data.comment: Error when changing a built-in fan profile. {0}: the profile name.

data.name: Library_NotFound
data.value: There is no custom profile named "{0}".
data.comment: Error when a custom fan profile does not exist. {0}: the name, made printable.

data.name: Library_DesiredSelected
data.value: This profile is currently selected; choose another profile before deleting it.
data.comment: Error when deleting the fan profile that is selected.

data.name: Library_CurvesMissing
data.value: The fan curve is incomplete.
data.comment: Error when a fan profile has no complete curves.

data.name: Name_Empty
data.value: The profile name cannot be empty.
data.comment: Error on a fan profile name.

data.name: Name_BadCharacters
data.value: The profile name cannot contain control or invalid characters.
data.comment: Error on a fan profile name: control characters, line breaks, text direction marks and lone surrogates are refused.

data.name: Name_TooLong
data.value: The profile name can be at most {0} characters ({1} given).
data.comment: Error on a fan profile name. {0}: the limit. {1}: the length of the name that was given.

data.name: Name_Taken
data.value: A profile named "{0}" already exists.
data.comment: Error on a fan profile name. {0}: the name.

data.name: Name_Unnamed
data.value: (unnamed)
data.comment: Stands in for a profile name that is missing, in a warning or error. Keep the parentheses.

data.name: Name_CopySuffix
data.value: copy
data.comment: Added to a profile name to name its copy ("Cool copy"), then with a number ("Cool copy 2"). Starts with a space. Keep it short: names are limited to 24 characters.

data.name: Profile_Unknown
data.value: Unknown fan profile: {0}
data.comment: Error when selecting a fan profile that does not exist. {0}: the name, made printable.

data.name: Profile_ChargeLimitRange
data.value: The charge limit must be {0}-{1}% (got {2}%).
data.comment: SAFETY. Error when the charge limit is out of range. {0} and {1}: lowest and highest allowed percent. {2}: the value that was given.

data.name: Profile_ChangeFailed
data.value: The profile could not be changed.
data.comment: Error when a profile change fails and no reason is known.

data.name: Settings_SaveFailed
data.value: Could not save the settings (settings.json: {0}); the previous settings return after a restart.
data.comment: Warning when settings.json cannot be written. {0}: the reason from the system or from M-Tool. settings.json is a file name.

data.name: Settings_UnknownProfile
data.value: Unknown fan profile ({0}); {1} is used.
data.comment: Settings warning when settings.json names a fan profile that does not exist. {0}: the name from the file, or the word for empty. {1}: the name of the profile used instead.

data.name: Settings_EmptyValue
data.value: empty
data.comment: Stands in for a missing name in a settings warning, shown in parentheses ("Unknown fan profile (empty)").

data.name: Settings_InvalidPerformanceMode
data.value: Invalid performance mode ({0}); ignored.
data.comment: Settings warning. {0}: the value from settings.json.

data.name: Settings_InvalidFanMode
data.value: Invalid fan mode ({0}); ignored.
data.comment: Settings warning. {0}: the value from settings.json.

data.name: Settings_InvalidChargeLimit
data.value: Invalid charge limit ({0}%); it must be {1}-{2}%, ignored.
data.comment: Settings warning. {0}: the value from settings.json, in percent. {1} and {2}: lowest and highest allowed percent.

data.name: Settings_PairMissingAc
data.value: The fan profile used on AC power was not found ({0}); the current setting is kept when switching to AC.
data.comment: Settings warning about the power-source switch. {0}: the name from the file, or the word for empty. AC = mains power.

data.name: Settings_PairMissingBattery
data.value: The fan profile used on battery power was not found ({0}); the current setting is kept when switching to battery.
data.comment: Settings warning about the power-source switch. {0}: the name from the file, or the word for empty.

data.name: Settings_ProfileDropped
data.value: Custom profile "{0}" was set aside: {1}.
data.comment: Settings warning. {0}: the profile name, made printable. {1}: the reason, a phrase without a final full stop (one of the Settings_Drop texts, or a name or curve problem).

data.name: Settings_ProfilesDroppedMore
data.value: {0} more custom profiles were set aside.
data.comment: Settings warning after the first ten dropped profiles were named. {0}: how many more.

data.name: Settings_DropTooMany
data.value: there can be at most {0} custom profiles
data.comment: Reason in Settings_ProfileDropped. {0}: the limit.

data.name: Settings_DropMissingPart
data.value: a field is missing.
data.comment: Reason in Settings_ProfileDropped. The final full stop is removed when the text is used.

data.name: Settings_DropNameNotNormal
data.value: the name was saved with spaces at its start or end, or with a decomposed letter.
data.comment: Reason in Settings_ProfileDropped. A decomposed letter is a base letter followed by a combining mark (for example C + cedilla instead of the single letter). The final full stop is removed when the text is used.

data.name: Settings_DropCurve
data.value: it breaks the fan rules ({0})
data.comment: Reason in Settings_ProfileDropped. {0}: the first problem, one of the Curve texts, without its final full stop.

data.name: Store_Unreadable
data.value: settings.json could not be read ({0}); defaults are used.
data.comment: Settings warning at start. {0}: the reason from the system. settings.json is a file name.

data.name: Store_UnreadableNotMoved
data.value: settings.json could not be read ({0}) and could not be set aside ({1}); defaults are used.
data.comment: Settings warning at start. {0}: why it could not be read. {1}: the reason from the system.

data.name: Store_SetAside
data.value: settings.json could not be read ({0}); it was kept as {1}, defaults are used.
data.comment: Settings warning at start. {0}: why it could not be read (one of the Store_Reason texts or a parser message). {1}: the file name of the kept copy.

data.name: Store_ReasonTooBig
data.value: larger than {0} KB
data.comment: Reason in Store_SetAside. {0}: the size limit in kilobytes.

data.name: Store_ReasonEmpty
data.value: empty or incomplete
data.comment: Reason in Store_SetAside.

data.name: Store_ReasonVersion
data.value: invalid version number: {0}
data.comment: Reason in Store_SetAside. {0}: the schema version number from the file.

data.name: Store_NewerVersion
data.value: settings.json belongs to a newer version of M-Tool; defaults are used and changes are not saved. Install the newer version.
data.comment: Settings warning at start.

data.name: Store_RefuseUnread
data.value: settings.json is not overwritten because it could not be read at start; restart M-Tool
data.comment: Reason given when a save is refused. It is shown inside Settings_SaveFailed, so it has no final full stop.

data.name: Store_RefuseNewer
data.value: settings.json belongs to a newer version of M-Tool, this version does not overwrite it; install the newer version
data.comment: Reason given when a save is refused. It is shown inside Settings_SaveFailed, so it has no final full stop.

data.name: Store_CopyKept
data.value: The previous version of settings.json was kept as {0}.
data.comment: Settings message at start. {0}: the file name of the copy.

data.name: Store_CopyFailed
data.value: A copy of settings.json could not be kept ({0}); the profiles that were set aside are lost at the next save.
data.comment: Settings warning at start. {0}: the reason from the system.

data.name: Write_Locked
data.value: Changing settings is turned off: {0}
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome shown when writes are locked, so nothing was written. {0}: why they are locked (one of the Write_Lock texts, or a reason saved by an earlier session).

data.name: Write_LockUnverifiedRecord
data.value: values are read with an unverified device record; restart M-Tool.
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Locked. The session fell back to a draft device record, so nothing may be written. Keep the name M-Tool.

data.name: Write_LockFirmware
data.value: this firmware is not supported (only {0}).
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Locked. {0}: the one firmware version M-Tool may write to. Keep the version unchanged.

data.name: Write_LockNoBackup
data.value: the settings backup taken at first launch is missing or damaged.
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Locked. The backup of the laptop's own settings, taken the first time M-Tool ran.

data.name: Write_LockFileUnreadable
data.value: the lock file (write-lock.txt) could not be read ({0}).
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Locked. An unreadable lock file counts as a lock. Keep the file name write-lock.txt. {0}: the reason from the system.

data.name: Write_LockAfterFailure
data.value: a previous setting could not be applied ({0}). Detail: {1}
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Locked, kept for later sessions. {0}: what was being applied (an English name, not translated). {1}: what went wrong (a Write text or a message from the system).

data.name: Write_Unreachable
data.value: Could not reach the laptop; no setting was changed. Try again in a moment. ({0})
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome when the laptop's controller could not be reached before anything was written. {0}: the reason from the system or from the controller worker (one of the Worker texts).

data.name: Write_EmptyPlan
data.value: The plan is empty.
data.comment: Outcome when there is nothing to write.

data.name: Write_DuplicateRegister
data.value: 0x{0:X2} appears more than once in the plan.
data.comment: Outcome when a register is listed twice. {0}: the register number, written in hexadecimal. Keep 0x and the format.

data.name: Write_PortUnavailable
data.value: {0}: Cooler Boost and the charge limit are not available in this session (no PawnIO access).
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome for a Cooler Boost or charge limit write without port access. {0}: the register and value, such as 0xEF=0xCF; keep it. Keep Cooler Boost and PawnIO.

data.name: Write_PortAlone
data.value: {0}: a port register must be the only write in its plan.
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome when a Cooler Boost or charge limit write comes with other writes. {0}: the register and value, such as 0xEF=0xCF; keep it.

data.name: Write_DryRun
data.value: Dry-run mode: checked, not applied.
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome in dry-run mode: the change was checked but nothing was written.

data.name: Write_Applied
data.value: Applied and verified.
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome when a change was written and read back correctly.

data.name: Write_ReadBackDiffers
data.value: The setting was written but read back differently ({0}).
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Failed. {0}: the register and value that did not stick, such as 0x72=0x32; keep it.

data.name: Write_OthersChanged
data.value: The setting was written but other values changed too; stopped for safety.
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Failed. A Cooler Boost or charge limit write changed other registers.

data.name: Write_ReadBackFailed
data.value: The setting was written but could not be read back ({0}).
data.comment: SAFETY. Reason in Write_Failed. {0}: the reason from the system.

data.name: Write_CurveUnsafe
data.value: The {0} curve would be unsafe: {1}
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome when a change would leave a fan curve breaking the safety rules. {0}: CPU or GPU, not translated. {1}: the first problem, one of the Curve texts.

data.name: Write_Failed
data.value: The setting could not be applied. {0}
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome after a failed write; writes are locked from then on. {0}: details (a reason, what happened to other registers, what was restored).

data.name: Write_Restored
data.value: Restored: {0}.
data.comment: SAFETY. Part of Write_Failed. {0}: the registers and values put back, such as 0xF2=0xC0; keep them.

data.name: Write_NotRestored
data.value: Could not be restored: {0}.
data.comment: SAFETY. Part of Write_Failed. {0}: the registers and values that could not be put back; keep them.

data.name: Write_PortRefused
data.value: {0} is not available in this session (no PawnIO access).
data.comment: SAFETY. Outcome for Cooler Boost without port access. {0}: the feature name; Cooler Boost is not translated. Keep PawnIO.

data.name: Worker_Paused
data.value: EC access is paused because of sleep or wake-up.
data.comment: Message when the laptop is asleep or just woke up, so its controller (EC) was not touched. It appears inside Write_Unreachable.

data.name: Worker_LockTimeout
data.value: The EC lock (Access_EC) was not obtained within {0} ms; another program may be using the EC.
data.comment: Message when the shared controller (EC) lock stayed taken. {0}: the time waited in milliseconds. Keep Access_EC. It appears inside Write_Unreachable.

data.name: Rule_NotWritable
data.value: 0x{0:X2} is not in the list of writable registers.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection when a write targets a register outside the whitelist, so nothing was written. {0}: the register number as two hex digits; keep the 0x prefix.

data.name: Rule_UpThreshold
data.value: {0}: the up threshold must be {1}-{2} °C.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a fan table up threshold outside the allowed range. {0}: the register and value, such as 0x6A=0x1D; keep it. {1}, {2}: lowest and highest allowed temperature.

data.name: Rule_SpeedMax
data.value: {0}: the fan speed is at most {1}%.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a fan speed above the maximum. {0}: the register and value; keep it. {1}: the highest allowed speed in percent.

data.name: Rule_ChargeLimit
data.value: {0}: the charge limit must be 0x80 | {1}-{2}%.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a charge limit value outside the allowed range. {0}: the register and value; keep it. Keep 0x80 | unchanged (bit 7 set plus the percent). {1}, {2}: lowest and highest allowed percent.

data.name: Rule_PerformanceMode
data.value: {0}: unsupported performance mode.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a performance mode value the laptop does not know. {0}: the register and value; keep it.

data.name: Rule_FanMode
data.value: {0}: unsupported fan mode.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a fan mode value the laptop does not know. {0}: the register and value; keep it.

data.name: Rule_KeyboardBacklight
data.value: {0}: unsupported keyboard backlight level.
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a keyboard backlight value outside the four levels (0x80-0x83). {0}: the register and value; keep it.

data.name: Rule_CoolerBoostBits
data.value: {0}: a Cooler Boost write may change only bit 7 (currently 0x{1:X2}).
data.comment: SAFETY. Rejection of a Cooler Boost write that would change bits other than the switch. {0}: the register and value; keep it. {1}: the value the register holds now, as two hex digits.

data.name: PortGuard_Unreadable
data.value: The watched registers could not be read after the port access.
data.comment: SAFETY. Part of the failure text when the registers watched during a port access cannot be read afterwards.

data.name: PortGuard_Changed
data.value: The port access changed other registers: {0}.
data.comment: SAFETY. Part of the failure text when a port access changed registers it should not touch. {0}: the registers and values, such as 0xF2=0xC4; keep them.
